Under token-level reweighting, the policy-gradient contribution at position (i,t)(i,t) is linearly scaled by a positive weight ωi,t\omega_{i,t}. Since the first-order entropy derivative in Theorem 3.1 is linear in the policy-gradient direction, the corresponding entropy contribution becomes

−ωi,t​A^i​Φi,t.-\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.

Hence the batch-averaged first-order entropy variation is

d​H¯d​η|ω=−1N∑i,tωi,tA^iΦi,t.\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\omega}=-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i,t}\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.

In the present reweighting scheme,

ωi,t={W,(i,t)∈ℒ+,1,otherwise.\omega_{i,t}=\begin{cases}W,&(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}

Therefore,

d​H¯d​η|W=−1N​[∑(i,t)∉ℒ+A^i​Φi,t+W​∑(i,t)∈ℒ+A^i​Φi,t].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{W}=-\frac{1}{N}\left[\sum_{(i,t)\notin\mathcal{L}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}+W\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\right].

Equivalently,

d​H¯d​η|W=−1N​[∑i,tA^i​Φi,t+(W−1)​∑(i,t)∈ℒ+A^i​Φi,t].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{W}=-\frac{1}{N}\left[\sum_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}+(W-1)\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\right].

Define

Λ≜∑i,tA^i​Φi,t.\Lambda\triangleq\sum_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.

For any (i,t)∈ℒ+(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+}, we have A^i>0\hat{A}_{i}>0 and 𝔰i,t>𝔰i,t∗\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}>\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}^{*}. By Proposition 3.2, Φi,t<0\Phi_{i,t}<0. Hence

A^i​Φi,t=−A^i​|Φi,t|.\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}=-\hat{A}_{i}|\Phi_{i,t}|.

It follows that

∑(i,t)∈ℒ+A^iΦi,t=−∑(i,t)∈ℒ+A^i|Φi,t|.\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}=-\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}|\Phi_{i,t}|.

Define

Γ≜∑(i,t)∈ℒ+A^i​|Φi,t|.\Gamma\triangleq\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}|\Phi_{i,t}|.

When ℒ+\mathcal{L}^{+} is nonempty, Γ>0\Gamma>0 because A^i>0\hat{A}_{i}>0 and |Φi,t|>0|\Phi_{i,t}|>0 on this set. The expression above becomes

d​H¯d​η|W=−1N​[Λ−(W−1)​Γ].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{W}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(W-1)\Gamma\Big].

sign⁡(d​H¯d​η|W)\displaystyle\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{W}\right) =−sign⁡(W∗−W)\displaystyle=-\operatorname{sign}(W^{*}-W)
=sign⁡(W−W∗).\displaystyle=\operatorname{sign}(W-W^{*}).

Thus d​H¯/d​η|W>0\left.d\bar{H}/d\eta\right|_{W}>0 when W>W∗W>W^{*}, d​H¯/d​η|W<0\left.d\bar{H}/d\eta\right|_{W}<0 when W<W∗W<W^{*}, and the first-order entropy variation is zero when W=W∗W=W^{*}. ∎

If a token satisfies

𝔰≥H,\mathfrak{s}\geq H,

|Φ⁡(p)|=−Φ⁡(p)=S2−p⁡(ln⁡p+H)≥S2.|\Phi(p)|=-\Phi(p)=S_{2}-p(\ln p+H)\geq S_{2}.

∎

p⁡(ln⁡p+H)=p​ln⁡p+p​H≤H.p(\ln p+H)=p\ln p+pH\leq H.

E.9 Statistical Assumptions for the Near-Criticality Analysis

E.9.1 Single-Token Credit Dilution

Assumption E.1 (Single-token credit dilution).

For long sequences and sufficiently large batches, define the conditional advantage function at any position (i,t)(i,t) as

gi,t(v)≜𝔼[A^i∣ci,t,oi,t=v].g_{i,t}(v)\triangleq\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\mid c_{i,t},\ o_{i,t}=v].

There exists a constant Cg>0C_{g}>0, independent of the sequence length TT, such that for every position and every u,v∈𝒱u,v\in\mathcal{V},

|gi,t​(u)−gi,t​(v)|≤CgT.|g_{i,t}(u)-g_{i,t}(v)|\leq\frac{C_{g}}{T}.

This assumption states that, along a trajectory of length TT, the marginal effect of any single token on the trajectory-level advantage is diluted at rate 1/T1/T.

E.9.2 Non-Degenerate Absolute Scale of the Advantage

Assumption E.2 (Non-degenerate absolute scale of the advantage).

There exists a constant a−>0a_{-}>0 such that, for every position (i,t)(i,t) and every candidate token vv,

𝔼[|A^i|∣ci,t,oi,t=v]≥a−.\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\hat{A}_{i}|\mid c_{i,t},\ o_{i,t}=v\bigr]\geq a_{-}.

This assumption states that the conditional absolute scale of the normalized advantage remains O⁡(1)O(1) rather than degenerating to zero.

E.9.3 Non-Vanishing Mass of a Strong High-Surprisal Positive-Advantage Subset

Assumption E.3 (Non-vanishing mass of a strong high-surprisal positive-advantage subset).

Define

ℋ+≜{(i,t):A^i>0,𝔰i,t≥Hi,t}.\mathcal{H}^{+}\triangleq\{(i,t):\hat{A}_{i}>0,\ \mathfrak{s}_{i,t}\geq H_{i,t}\}.

There exist constants ρH>0\rho_{H}>0 and cH>0c_{H}>0 such that, for sufficiently large batches, with high probability,

|ℋ+|≥ρH​N,|\mathcal{H}^{+}|\geq\rho_{H}N,

and

1|ℋ+|​∑(i,t)∈ℋ+A^i​S2,i,t≥cH.\frac{1}{|\mathcal{H}^{+}|}\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{H}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}S_{2,i,t}\geq c_{H}.

E.9.4 Linear Scale of Total Absolute Entropy Sensitivity

Assumption E.4 (Linear scale of total absolute entropy sensitivity).

Let

Σabs≜∑i,t|A^i|​|Φi,t|.\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}\triangleq\sum_{i,t}|\hat{A}_{i}|\,|\Phi_{i,t}|.

There exists a constant cΣ<∞c_{\Sigma}<\infty such that, for sufficiently large batches, with high probability,

Σabs≤cΣ​N.\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}\leq c_{\Sigma}N.

E.10 Λ\Lambda Is a Weak Residual

Lemma E.5 (Λ\Lambda is a weak residual).

Under Assumptions E.1 and E.2, and under standard large-batch concentration with uniformly bounded second moments,

|Λ|Σabs=O⁡(T−1),Λ≜∑i,tA^i​Φi,t.\frac{|\Lambda|}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}=O(T^{-1}),\qquad\Lambda\triangleq\sum_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.
Proof.

The proof first establishes the O⁡(T−1)O(T^{-1}) scaling at the population level and then transfers it to empirical batch quantities by concentration.

Fix a position (i,t)(i,t) and condition on ci,t=cc_{i,t}=c. Define

Φc​(v)≜πθ​(v∣c)​(ln⁡πθ​(v∣c)+H⁡(c))−S2​(c).\Phi_{c}(v)\triangleq\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)\bigl(\ln\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)+H(c)\bigr)-S_{2}(c).

When the sampled token is oi,to_{i,t},

Φi,t=Φc​(oi,t).\Phi_{i,t}=\Phi_{c}(o_{i,t}).

By the law of total expectation,

𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t]=𝔼⁡[𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t∣ci,t]].\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}]=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\mid c_{i,t}]\right].

Given ci,t=cc_{i,t}=c, the token oi,to_{i,t} is sampled from πθ(⋅∣c)\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid c). Thus

𝔼[A^iΦi,t∣ci,t=c]=∑v∈𝒱πθ(v∣c)𝔼[A^i∣ci,t=c,oi,t=v]Φc(v).\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\mid c_{i,t}=c]=\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\mid c_{i,t}=c,\ o_{i,t}=v]\Phi_{c}(v).

Let

gc(v)≜𝔼[A^i∣ci,t=c,oi,t=v].g_{c}(v)\triangleq\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\mid c_{i,t}=c,\ o_{i,t}=v].

Then

𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t∣ci,t=c]=∑vπθ​(v∣c)​gc​(v)​Φc​(v).\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\mid c_{i,t}=c]=\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)g_{c}(v)\Phi_{c}(v).

We now use the Entropy Neutrality Identity to remove the mean component of gcg_{c}. Define

g¯c≜∑vπθ​(v∣c)​gc​(v).\bar{g}_{c}\triangleq\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)g_{c}(v).

By Theorem 3.4,

∑vπθ​(v∣c)​Φc​(v)=0.\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)\Phi_{c}(v)=0.

Therefore,

∑vπθ​(v∣c)​gc​(v)​Φc​(v)=∑vπθ​(v∣c)​(gc​(v)−g¯c)​Φc​(v),\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)g_{c}(v)\Phi_{c}(v)=\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)\bigl(g_{c}(v)-\bar{g}_{c}\bigr)\Phi_{c}(v),

which implies

𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t∣ci,t=c]=∑vπθ​(v∣c)​(gc​(v)−g¯c)​Φc​(v).\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\mid c_{i,t}=c]=\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)\bigl(g_{c}(v)-\bar{g}_{c}\bigr)\Phi_{c}(v).

Since g¯c\bar{g}_{c} is a πθ(⋅∣c)\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid c)-weighted average of {gc​(v)}v∈𝒱\{g_{c}(v)\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}}, for every vv,

|gc​(v)−g¯c|≤maxu,v′⁡|gc​(u)−gc​(v′)|.|g_{c}(v)-\bar{g}_{c}|\leq\max_{u,v^{\prime}}|g_{c}(u)-g_{c}(v^{\prime})|.

Assumption E.1 gives

|gc​(v)−g¯c|≤CgT.|g_{c}(v)-\bar{g}_{c}|\leq\frac{C_{g}}{T}.

Consequently,

|𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t∣ci,t=c]|≤CgT​∑vπθ​(v∣c)​|Φc​(v)|.\left|\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\mid c_{i,t}=c]\right|\leq\frac{C_{g}}{T}\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)|\Phi_{c}(v)|.

Define

Ψ⁡(c)≜∑vπθ​(v∣c)​|Φc​(v)|.\Psi(c)\triangleq\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)|\Phi_{c}(v)|.

Then

|𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t∣ci,t=c]|≤CgT​Ψ​(c).\left|\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\mid c_{i,t}=c]\right|\leq\frac{C_{g}}{T}\Psi(c).

Summing over all token positions yields

|𝔼⁡[Λ]|=|∑i,t𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t]|≤∑i,t|𝔼⁡[A^i​Φi,t]|≤CgT​∑i,t𝔼⁡[Ψ⁡(ci,t)].|\mathbb{E}[\Lambda]|=\left|\sum_{i,t}\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}]\right|\leq\sum_{i,t}\left|\mathbb{E}[\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}]\right|\leq\frac{C_{g}}{T}\sum_{i,t}\mathbb{E}[\Psi(c_{i,t})].

We next lower bound 𝔼⁡[Σabs]\mathbb{E}[\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}]. Conditional on ci,t=cc_{i,t}=c,

𝔼[|A^i||Φi,t|∣ci,t=c]=∑vπθ(v∣c)𝔼[|A^i|∣ci,t=c,oi,t=v]|Φc(v)|.\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\hat{A}_{i}|\,|\Phi_{i,t}|\mid c_{i,t}=c\bigr]=\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\hat{A}_{i}|\mid c_{i,t}=c,\ o_{i,t}=v\bigr]|\Phi_{c}(v)|.

By Assumption E.2,

𝔼[|A^i|∣ci,t=c,oi,t=v]≥a−.\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\hat{A}_{i}|\mid c_{i,t}=c,\ o_{i,t}=v\bigr]\geq a_{-}.

Therefore,

𝔼⁡[|A^i|​|Φi,t|∣ci,t=c]≥a−​∑vπθ​(v∣c)|Φc​(v)|=a−​Ψ​(c).\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\hat{A}_{i}|\,|\Phi_{i,t}|\mid c_{i,t}=c\bigr]\geq a_{-}\sum_{v}\pi_{\theta}(v\mid c)|\Phi_{c}(v)|=a_{-}\Psi(c).

Summing over positions and taking expectations gives

𝔼⁡[Σabs]=∑i,t𝔼⁡[|A^i|​|Φi,t|]≥a−​∑i,t𝔼⁡[Ψ⁡(ci,t)].\mathbb{E}[\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}]=\sum_{i,t}\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\hat{A}_{i}|\,|\Phi_{i,t}|\bigr]\geq a_{-}\sum_{i,t}\mathbb{E}[\Psi(c_{i,t})].

Combining the upper bound on |𝔼⁡[Λ]||\mathbb{E}[\Lambda]| and the lower bound on 𝔼⁡[Σabs]\mathbb{E}[\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}] gives

|𝔼⁡[Λ]|𝔼⁡[Σabs]≤Cga−​T.\frac{|\mathbb{E}[\Lambda]|}{\mathbb{E}[\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}]}\leq\frac{C_{g}}{a_{-}T}.

Thus, at the population level,

|𝔼⁡[Λ]|𝔼⁡[Σabs]=O⁡(T−1).\frac{|\mathbb{E}[\Lambda]|}{\mathbb{E}[\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}]}=O(T^{-1}).

For sufficiently large batches, and assuming uniformly bounded second moments of the corresponding summands, Λ\Lambda and Σabs\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}} concentrate around their population values at a scale that does not change the dependence on TT. Hence, with high probability,

|Λ|Σabs=O⁡(T−1).\frac{|\Lambda|}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}=O(T^{-1}).

∎

E.11 Theorem 3.6 (Near-Criticality)

If Assumptions E.1–E.4 hold and both the sequence length TT and the batch size are sufficiently large, then

W∗−1=ΛΓ=O⁡(T−1).W^{*}-1=\frac{\Lambda}{\Gamma}=O(T^{-1}).
Proof.

By Proposition 3.5,

W∗−1=ΛΓ.W^{*}-1=\frac{\Lambda}{\Gamma}.

It remains to control the numerator and denominator.

For the numerator, Lemma E.5 gives

|Λ|Σabs=O⁡(T−1).\frac{|\Lambda|}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}=O(T^{-1}).

For the denominator, we show that Γ\Gamma is lower bounded by a constant-order fraction of the total absolute entropy sensitivity. First, ℋ+⊂ℒ+\mathcal{H}^{+}\subset\mathcal{L}^{+}. Indeed, Proposition 3.2 gives, at every position,

𝔰i,t∗<Hi,t.\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}^{*}<H_{i,t}.

Therefore, any token satisfying 𝔰i,t≥Hi,t\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}\geq H_{i,t} also satisfies

𝔰i,t>𝔰i,t∗.\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}>\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}^{*}.

Together with A^i>0\hat{A}_{i}>0, this implies

ℋ+⊂ℒ+.\mathcal{H}^{+}\subset\mathcal{L}^{+}.

By the definition of Γ\Gamma and the inclusion above,

Γ=∑(i,t)∈ℒ+A^i​|Φi,t|≥∑(i,t)∈ℋ+A^i​|Φi,t|.\Gamma=\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}|\Phi_{i,t}|\geq\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{H}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}|\Phi_{i,t}|.

On ℋ+\mathcal{H}^{+}, the condition 𝔰i,t≥Hi,t\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}\geq H_{i,t} holds. Lemma E.3 therefore gives

|Φi,t|≥S2,i,t.|\Phi_{i,t}|\geq S_{2,i,t}.

Hence

Γ≥∑(i,t)∈ℋ+A^i​S2,i,t.\Gamma\geq\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{H}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}S_{2,i,t}.

By Assumption E.3,

1|ℋ+|​∑(i,t)∈ℋ+A^i​S2,i,t≥cH,|ℋ+|≥ρH​N.\frac{1}{|\mathcal{H}^{+}|}\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{H}^{+}}\hat{A}_{i}S_{2,i,t}\geq c_{H},\qquad|\mathcal{H}^{+}|\geq\rho_{H}N.

Therefore,

Γ≥cH​|ℋ+|≥cH​ρH​N.\Gamma\geq c_{H}|\mathcal{H}^{+}|\geq c_{H}\rho_{H}N.

Assumption E.4 gives

Σabs≤cΣ​N.\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}\leq c_{\Sigma}N.

Consequently,

ΣabsΓ≤cΣ​NcH​ρH​N=cΣcH​ρH=O⁡(1).\frac{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}{\Gamma}\leq\frac{c_{\Sigma}N}{c_{H}\rho_{H}N}=\frac{c_{\Sigma}}{c_{H}\rho_{H}}=O(1).

We now decompose the critical offset as

ΛΓ=ΛΣabs⋅ΣabsΓ.\frac{\Lambda}{\Gamma}=\frac{\Lambda}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}\cdot\frac{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}{\Gamma}.

Taking absolute values gives

|ΛΓ|=|Λ|Σabs⋅ΣabsΓ.\left|\frac{\Lambda}{\Gamma}\right|=\frac{|\Lambda|}{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}\cdot\frac{\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}}{\Gamma}.

The first factor is O⁡(T−1)O(T^{-1}) by Lemma E.5, and the second factor is O⁡(1)O(1) by the bound above. Hence

|ΛΓ|=O⁡(T−1).\left|\frac{\Lambda}{\Gamma}\right|=O(T^{-1}).

Equivalently,

W∗−1=ΛΓ=O⁡(T−1).W^{*}-1=\frac{\Lambda}{\Gamma}=O(T^{-1}).

∎

In the entropy-collapse regime studied in the main text, baseline GRPO corresponds to Λ>0\Lambda>0. Hence W∗>1W^{*}>1, and the critical weight exceeds one only by an O⁡(T−1)O(T^{-1}) offset. The proof lower bounds Γ\Gamma using the stronger subset ℋ+\mathcal{H}^{+} rather than the full entropy-increasing positive-advantage set ℒ+\mathcal{L}^{+}, so the argument is conservative. In actual training, additional contributions from ℒ+∖ℋ+\mathcal{L}^{+}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{+} further enlarge Γ\Gamma and make the critical offset closer to zero.

Appendix F Formalization of the Cross-Step Entropy Dynamics in Section 3.4

This appendix casts the dynamical discussion in Section 3.4 as a discrete-time system under a mean-field closure. The purpose is to formalize the qualitative mechanism described in the main text. It is not intended as an unconditional global convergence theorem for general deep neural network training.

F.1 Mean-Field Approximation

Assume that, within the training interval of interest, the batch-level quantities Λk\Lambda_{k} and Γk\Gamma_{k} are primarily determined by the current batch-averaged policy entropy H¯k\bar{H}_{k}. More precisely, suppose that there exist continuous functions Λ⁡(h)\Lambda(h) and Γ⁡(h)\Gamma(h) such that

Λk≈Λ⁡(H¯k),Γk≈Γ⁡(H¯k),Γ⁡(h)>0.\Lambda_{k}\approx\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k}),\qquad\Gamma_{k}\approx\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k}),\qquad\Gamma(h)>0.

The associated critical-weight curve is defined as

W∗​(h)≜1+Λ⁡(h)Γ⁡(h).W^{*}(h)\triangleq 1+\frac{\Lambda(h)}{\Gamma(h)}.

The statement in the main text that flatter policy distributions require a lower critical weight to sustain entropy growth is formalized through the following monotonicity condition:

W∗​(h)​is strictly decreasing in ​h​ on the relevant interval.W^{*}(h)\ \text{is strictly decreasing in }h\text{ on the relevant interval.}

F.2 Sign of the One-Step Batch Entropy Change under a Fixed Weight

Proposition F.1 (Sign of the one-step batch entropy change under a fixed weight).

For a fixed token-level reweighting factor WW, the one-step change in batch-averaged policy entropy satisfies

Δ​H¯k=−1N​[Λ⁡(H¯k)−(W−1)​Γ​(H¯k)]=Γ⁡(H¯k)N​[W−W∗​(H¯k)].\Delta\bar{H}_{k}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k})-(W-1)\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})\Big]=\frac{\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})}{N}\Big[W-W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})\Big].

Consequently,

sign⁡(Δ​H¯k)=sign⁡(W−W∗​(H¯k)).\operatorname{sign}(\Delta\bar{H}_{k})=\operatorname{sign}\bigl(W-W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})\bigr).
Proof.

By the mean-field form of the batch-level entropy dynamics,

Δ​H¯k=−1N​[Λ⁡(H¯k)−(W−1)​Γ​(H¯k)].\Delta\bar{H}_{k}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k})-(W-1)\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})\Big].

The bracketed term can be rewritten as

Λ⁡(H¯k)−(W−1)​Γ​(H¯k)=Γ⁡(H¯k)​[Λ⁡(H¯k)Γ⁡(H¯k)−(W−1)].\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k})-(W-1)\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})=\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})\left[\frac{\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k})}{\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})}-(W-1)\right].

Since

W∗​(H¯k)=1+Λ⁡(H¯k)Γ⁡(H¯k),W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})=1+\frac{\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k})}{\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})},

we have

Λ⁡(H¯k)Γ⁡(H¯k)−(W−1)=W∗​(H¯k)−W.\frac{\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k})}{\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})}-(W-1)=W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})-W.

Substituting this identity gives

Δ​H¯k=−Γ⁡(H¯k)N​[W∗​(H¯k)−W]=Γ⁡(H¯k)N​[W−W∗​(H¯k)].\Delta\bar{H}_{k}=-\frac{\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})}{N}\bigl[W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})-W\bigr]=\frac{\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})}{N}\bigl[W-W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})\bigr].

Because N>0N>0 and Γ⁡(H¯k)>0\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})>0, the sign of Δ​H¯k\Delta\bar{H}_{k} is entirely determined by W−W∗​(H¯k)W-W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k}). This proves the proposition. ∎

F.3 Open-Loop Self-Reinforcing Entropy Collapse and Recovery

Corollary F.2 (Open-loop self-reinforcing entropy collapse and recovery).

Under the mean-field approximation above, the open-loop dynamics exhibit two symmetric feedback regimes. If W=1W=1 and the current entropy level satisfies W∗​(H¯k)>1W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})>1, then Proposition F.1 gives Δ​H¯k<0\Delta\bar{H}_{k}<0. Since W∗​(h)W^{*}(h) is strictly decreasing in hh, the next step satisfies

H¯k+1<H¯k⟹W∗​(H¯k+1)≥W∗​(H¯k).\bar{H}_{k+1}<\bar{H}_{k}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k+1})\geq W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k}).

Thus, the unit-weight GRPO baseline moves farther below the critical-weight curve, which strengthens the entropy-decreasing pressure and reinforces entropy collapse.

Conversely, if at some step W>W∗​(H¯k)W>W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k}), then Proposition F.1 gives Δ​H¯k>0\Delta\bar{H}_{k}>0. By the same monotonicity condition,

H¯k+1>H¯k⟹W∗​(H¯k+1)≤W∗​(H¯k).\bar{H}_{k+1}>\bar{H}_{k}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k+1})\leq W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k}).

Therefore, the margin by which the fixed weight exceeds the critical-weight curve increases after the entropy rises. The entropy-increasing pressure is consequently strengthened, which reinforces entropy recovery.

Proof.

Both claims follow from Proposition F.1 and the monotonicity of W∗​(h)W^{*}(h). For the collapse regime, if W=1W=1 and W∗​(H¯k)>1W^{*}(\bar{H}_{k})>1, then Δ​H¯k<0\Delta\bar{H}_{k}<0, so H¯k+1<H¯k\bar{H}_{k+1}<\bar{H}_{k}. Since the critical-weight curve decreases with entropy, evaluating it at the smaller entropy value H¯k+1\bar{H}_{k+1} yields a critical weight that is no smaller than before. The unit-weight baseline is therefore even farther below the critical threshold at the next step. The recovery regime follows by the same argument with the inequalities reversed. This proves the corollary. ∎

F.4 Local Stability of Batch-Level Target-Entropy Gating

Proposition F.3 (Local stability of batch-level target-entropy gating).

Consider the batch-level target-entropy gating rule introduced in Section 4.3,

gk=𝟏[H¯k<Htgt].g_{k}=\mathbf{1}[\bar{H}_{k}<H_{\mathrm{tgt}}].

For the one-sided STARE variant, the one-step change in batch-averaged policy entropy is

Δ​H¯k=−1N​[Λ⁡(H¯k)−gk​(W−1)​Γ​(H¯k)].\Delta\bar{H}_{k}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda(\bar{H}_{k})-g_{k}(W-1)\Gamma(\bar{H}_{k})\Big].

Define the gated and ungated update maps as

Fon​(h)≜−1N​[Λ⁡(h)−(W−1)​Γ​(h)],F_{\mathrm{on}}(h)\triangleq-\frac{1}{N}\big[\Lambda(h)-(W-1)\Gamma(h)\big],
Foff​(h)≜−1N​Λ​(h).F_{\mathrm{off}}(h)\triangleq-\frac{1}{N}\Lambda(h).

Assume that there exists a target-entropy neighborhood

I=[Htgt−δ,Htgt+δ]I=[H_{\mathrm{tgt}}-\delta,\ H_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\delta]

such that the gated update points toward higher entropy below the target, while the ungated update points toward lower entropy at and above the target:

Fon(h)>0,h∈[Htgt−δ,Htgt),F_{\mathrm{on}}(h)>0,\qquad h\in[H_{\mathrm{tgt}}-\delta,H_{\mathrm{tgt}}),
Foff​(h)<0,h∈[Htgt,Htgt+δ].F_{\mathrm{off}}(h)<0,\qquad h\in[H_{\mathrm{tgt}},H_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\delta].

Assume in addition that the one-step displacement inside this neighborhood is bounded by the neighborhood half-width:

Δmax≜max{suph∈[Htgt−δ,Htgt)Fon(h),suph∈[Htgt,Htgt+δ]|Foff(h)|}≤δ.\Delta_{\max}\triangleq\max\Bigg\{\sup_{h\in[H_{\mathrm{tgt}}-\delta,H_{\mathrm{tgt}})}F_{\mathrm{on}}(h),\ \sup_{h\in[H_{\mathrm{tgt}},H_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\delta]}|F_{\mathrm{off}}(h)|\Bigg\}\leq\delta.

Then II is forward invariant for the induced discrete-time entropy dynamics. Equivalently, once H¯k\bar{H}_{k} enters II, all subsequent batch-averaged entropy values remain inside this neighborhood. The closed-loop system therefore exhibits bounded oscillation around the target entropy, rather than continuing to drift monotonically away from it.

Proof.

Within II, the assumed sign conditions imply

Fon​(h)>0(h<Htgt),Foff​(h)<0(h≥Htgt).F_{\mathrm{on}}(h)>0\quad(h<H_{\mathrm{tgt}}),\qquad F_{\mathrm{off}}(h)<0\quad(h\geq H_{\mathrm{tgt}}).

The bounded-step condition gives Δmax≤δ\Delta_{\max}\leq\delta.

If H¯k∈[Htgt−δ,Htgt)\bar{H}_{k}\in[H_{\mathrm{tgt}}-\delta,H_{\mathrm{tgt}}), then gk=1g_{k}=1, and hence

H¯k+1=H¯k+Fon​(H¯k).\bar{H}_{k+1}=\bar{H}_{k}+F_{\mathrm{on}}(\bar{H}_{k}).

Since Fon​(H¯k)>0F_{\mathrm{on}}(\bar{H}_{k})>0,

H¯k+1>H¯k≥Htgt−δ.\bar{H}_{k+1}>\bar{H}_{k}\geq H_{\mathrm{tgt}}-\delta.

Moreover, Fon​(H¯k)≤Δmax≤δF_{\mathrm{on}}(\bar{H}_{k})\leq\Delta_{\max}\leq\delta, so

H¯k+1≤H¯k+δ<Htgt+δ.\bar{H}_{k+1}\leq\bar{H}_{k}+\delta<H_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\delta.

Therefore,

H¯k+1∈I.\bar{H}_{k+1}\in I.

If H¯k∈[Htgt,Htgt+δ]\bar{H}_{k}\in[H_{\mathrm{tgt}},H_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\delta], then gk=0g_{k}=0, and hence

H¯k+1=H¯k+Foff​(H¯k).\bar{H}_{k+1}=\bar{H}_{k}+F_{\mathrm{off}}(\bar{H}_{k}).

Since Foff​(H¯k)<0F_{\mathrm{off}}(\bar{H}_{k})<0,

H¯k+1<H¯k≤Htgt+δ.\bar{H}_{k+1}<\bar{H}_{k}\leq H_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\delta.

At the same time, |Foff​(H¯k)|≤Δmax≤δ|F_{\mathrm{off}}(\bar{H}_{k})|\leq\Delta_{\max}\leq\delta, which gives

H¯k+1≥H¯k−δ≥Htgt−δ.\bar{H}_{k+1}\geq\bar{H}_{k}-\delta\geq H_{\mathrm{tgt}}-\delta.

Thus,

H¯k+1∈I.\bar{H}_{k+1}\in I.

In both cases, one step of the dynamics maps II into itself. Hence II is forward invariant, and any trajectory that enters the target-entropy neighborhood remains there thereafter. This proves the proposition. ∎

Appendix G Single-Polarity Operations and Finer-Grained Closed-Loop Extensions

G.1 Definition of Surprisal-Quantile Proxy Sets

In Section 4.1 of the main text, we define

𝒯+={(i,t):A^i>0},𝒯−={(i,t):A^i<0}.\mathcal{T}^{+}=\{(i,t):\hat{A}_{i}>0\},\qquad\mathcal{T}^{-}=\{(i,t):\hat{A}_{i}<0\}.

Within 𝒯+\mathcal{T}^{+} and 𝒯−\mathcal{T}^{-}, token positions are sorted separately in descending order of surprisal,

𝔰i,t=−ln⁡πθ​(oi,t∣xi,oi,<t),\mathfrak{s}_{i,t}=-\ln\pi_{\theta}(o_{i,t}\mid x_{i},o_{i,<t}),

and the top P%P\% positions are selected to form

ℒq+⊂𝒯+,ℒq−⊂𝒯−.\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}\subset\mathcal{T}^{+},\qquad\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}\subset\mathcal{T}^{-}.

To cover all four single-polarity operations, we also define the corresponding low-surprisal proxy sets. Let 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} denote the bottom P%P\% positions with the lowest surprisal in 𝒯+\mathcal{T}^{+}, and let 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-} denote the bottom P%P\% positions with the lowest surprisal in 𝒯−\mathcal{T}^{-}.

These four proxy sets approximate the four theoretical quadrants in the advantage-surprisal decomposition. The set ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} corresponds to positive-advantage high-surprisal positions and targets the entropy-increasing quadrant. The set 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} corresponds to positive-advantage low-surprisal positions and targets the entropy-decreasing quadrant. The set 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-} corresponds to negative-advantage low-surprisal positions and targets the entropy-increasing quadrant. The set ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-} corresponds to negative-advantage high-surprisal positions and targets the entropy-decreasing quadrant.

G.2 Position-Level Logit Update under STARE Reweighting

Proposition G.1 (Position-level logit update under STARE reweighting).

Under the weighted clipped surrogate objective

𝒥STARE​(θ)=1N​∑i,tωi,t​min⁡(ρi,t​(θ)​A^i,clip⁡(ρi,t​(θ),1−ϵ,1+ϵ)​A^i),\mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{STARE}}(\theta)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i,t}\omega_{i,t}\min\!\Big(\rho_{i,t}(\theta)\hat{A}_{i},\,\operatorname{clip}(\rho_{i,t}(\theta),1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon)\hat{A}_{i}\Big),

if position (i,t)(i,t) lies in the unclipped regime, its effective logit update is

Δ​zv=η​ωi,t​A^i​(δv​a−πv),v∈𝒱.\Delta z_{v}=\eta\,\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}(\delta_{va}-\pi_{v}),\qquad v\in\mathcal{V}.

Since ωi,t>0\omega_{i,t}>0 always holds, STARE never reverses any token-level policy-gradient direction. It only selectively rescales the magnitude of the original GRPO learning signal.

Proof.

The proof follows the same argument as Proposition D.2. The only change is that the local surrogate term is multiplied by the positive weight ωi,t\omega_{i,t}. Therefore, the corresponding logit gradient is scaled by ωi,t\omega_{i,t}:

∂∂zv​[ωi,t​A^i​log⁡πa]=ωi,t​A^i​(δv​a−πv).\frac{\partial}{\partial z_{v}}\bigl[\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\log\pi_{a}\bigr]=\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}(\delta_{va}-\pi_{v}).

Taking one infinitesimal gradient ascent step gives the stated update. Because ωi,t>0\omega_{i,t}>0, the policy-gradient direction is preserved. This proves the proposition. ∎

G.3 Exact Batch-Level Entropy Variation under Reweighting an Arbitrary Token Subset

Proposition G.2 (Exact batch-level entropy variation under reweighting an arbitrary token subset).

Let 𝒮\mathcal{S} be an arbitrary subset of token positions. Apply a uniform weight r>0r>0 to positions in 𝒮\mathcal{S} and unit weight to all remaining positions:

ωi,t={r,(i,t)∈𝒮,1,otherwise.\omega_{i,t}=\begin{cases}r,&(i,t)\in\mathcal{S},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}

Then, in the unclipped regime,

d​H¯d​η|𝒮,r=−1N​[Λ+(r−1)​Ξ​(𝒮)],\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathcal{S},r}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(r-1)\Xi(\mathcal{S})\Big],

where

Λ≜∑i,tA^i​Φi,t,Ξ⁡(𝒮)≜∑(i,t)∈𝒮A^i​Φi,t.\Lambda\triangleq\sum_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t},\qquad\Xi(\mathcal{S})\triangleq\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{S}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.
Proof.

By Proposition G.1 and Theorem 3.1, the first-order entropy contribution at each position is linearly scaled by its token-level weight:

−ωi,t​A^i​Φi,t.-\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.

Thus,

d​H¯d​η|ω=−1N∑i,tωi,tA^iΦi,t.\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\omega}=-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i,t}\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.

Substituting the single-subset reweighting form gives

∑i,tωi,t​A^i​Φi,t=∑(i,t)∉𝒮A^i​Φi,t+r​∑(i,t)∈𝒮A^i​Φi,t.\sum_{i,t}\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}=\sum_{(i,t)\notin\mathcal{S}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}+r\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{S}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.

Rearranging the expression into the unweighted batch sum plus the reweighting correction yields

∑i,tωi,t​A^i​Φi,t=∑i,tA^i​Φi,t+(r−1)​∑(i,t)∈𝒮A^i​Φi,t=Λ+(r−1)​Ξ​(𝒮).\sum_{i,t}\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}=\sum_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}+(r-1)\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{S}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}=\Lambda+(r-1)\Xi(\mathcal{S}).

Substitution completes the proof:

d​H¯d​η|𝒮,r=−1N​[Λ+(r−1)​Ξ​(𝒮)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathcal{S},r}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(r-1)\Xi(\mathcal{S})\Big].

∎

G.4 Four Single-Polarity Operations

Operation O1 amplifies ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}. Define

ωi,t(O1)={W+,(i,t)∈ℒq+,1,otherwise,W+>1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{O1})}=\begin{cases}W_{+},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad W_{+}>1.

By Proposition G.2,

d​H¯d​η|O1=−1N​[Λ+(W+−1)​Ξ​(ℒq+)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O1}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(W_{+}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+})\Big].

When ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} is dominated by positive-advantage high-surprisal entropy-increasing positions, we have Ξ⁡(ℒq+)<0\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+})<0. Define

ΓL+≜−Ξ⁡(ℒq+)=∑(i,t)∈ℒq+|A^i​Φi,t|.\Gamma_{L^{+}}\triangleq-\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+})=\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}}|\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}|.

Then,

d​H¯d​η|O1=−1N​[Λ−(W+−1)​ΓL+].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O1}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(W_{+}-1)\Gamma_{L^{+}}\Big].

Operation O2 attenuates 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+}. Define

ωi,t(O2)={M+,(i,t)∈𝒰q+,1,otherwise,0<M+<1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{O2})}=\begin{cases}M_{+},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad 0<M_{+}<1.

By Proposition G.2,

d​H¯d​η|O2=−1N​[Λ+(M+−1)​Ξ​(𝒰q+)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O2}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(M_{+}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+})\Big].

When 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} is dominated by positive-advantage low-surprisal entropy-decreasing positions, we have Ξ⁡(𝒰q+)>0\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+})>0. Define

ΓU+≜Ξ⁡(𝒰q+)=∑(i,t)∈𝒰q+|A^i​Φi,t|.\Gamma_{U^{+}}\triangleq\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+})=\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+}}|\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}|.

Then,

d​H¯d​η|O2=−1N​[Λ−(1−M+)​ΓU+].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O2}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(1-M_{+})\Gamma_{U^{+}}\Big].

Operation O3 amplifies 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-}. Define

ωi,t(O3)={W−,(i,t)∈𝒰q−,1,otherwise,W−>1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{O3})}=\begin{cases}W_{-},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad W_{-}>1.

By Proposition G.2,

d​H¯d​η|O3=−1N​[Λ+(W−−1)​Ξ​(𝒰q−)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O3}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(W_{-}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-})\Big].

When 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-} is dominated by negative-advantage low-surprisal entropy-increasing positions, we have Ξ⁡(𝒰q−)<0\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-})<0. Define

ΓU−≜−Ξ⁡(𝒰q−)=∑(i,t)∈𝒰q−|A^i​Φi,t|.\Gamma_{U^{-}}\triangleq-\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-})=\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-}}|\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}|.

Then,

d​H¯d​η|O3=−1N​[Λ−(W−−1)​ΓU−].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O3}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(W_{-}-1)\Gamma_{U^{-}}\Big].

Operation O4 attenuates ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}. Define

ωi,t(O4)={M−,(i,t)∈ℒq−,1,otherwise,0<M−<1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{O4})}=\begin{cases}M_{-},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad 0<M_{-}<1.

By Proposition G.2,

d​H¯d​η|O4=−1N​[Λ+(M−−1)​Ξ​(ℒq−)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O4}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(M_{-}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-})\Big].

When ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-} is dominated by negative-advantage high-surprisal entropy-decreasing positions, we have Ξ⁡(ℒq−)>0\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-})>0. Define

ΓL−≜Ξ⁡(ℒq−)=∑(i,t)∈ℒq−|A^i​Φi,t|.\Gamma_{L^{-}}\triangleq\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-})=\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}}|\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}|.

Then,

d​H¯d​η|O4=−1N​[Λ−(1−M−)​ΓL−].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{O4}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(1-M_{-})\Gamma_{L^{-}}\Big].

G.5 Exact Entropy Variation under Unified Closed-Loop Gating

Proposition G.3 (Exact entropy variation under unified closed-loop gating).

Let gi,t∈{0,1}g_{i,t}\in\{0,1\} be an arbitrary binary gate. For the one-sided variant, define

ωi,t(V1,g)=1+gi,t(W−1)𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq+],W>1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{V1},g)}=1+g_{i,t}(W-1)\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}],\qquad W>1.

Then,

d​H¯d​η|V1,g=−1N[Λ+(W−1)∑i,tgi,t𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq+]A^iΦi,t].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{V1},g}=-\frac{1}{N}\left[\Lambda+(W-1)\sum_{i,t}g_{i,t}\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}]\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\right].

If the activated proxy set is dominated by the corresponding entropy-increasing quadrant, the expression reduces to

d​H¯d​η|V1,g=−1N​[Λ−(W−1)​Γg+],\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{V1},g}=-\frac{1}{N}\bigl[\Lambda-(W-1)\Gamma_{g}^{+}\bigr],

where

Γg+≜∑i,tgi,t𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq+]|A^iΦi,t|.\Gamma_{g}^{+}\triangleq\sum_{i,t}g_{i,t}\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}]|\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}|.

For the two-sided variant, define

ωi,t(V2,g)=1+gi,t(W−1)𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq+]−gi,t(1−M)𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq−],W>1,0<M<1.\displaystyle\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{V2},g)}=1+g_{i,t}(W-1)\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}]-g_{i,t}(1-M)\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}],\qquad W>1,\quad 0<M<1.

Then,

d​H¯d​η|V2,g=−1N[Λ+(W−1)∑i,tgi,t𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq+]A^iΦi,t+(M−1)∑i,tgi,t𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq−]A^iΦi,t].\displaystyle\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{V2},g}=-\frac{1}{N}\left[\Lambda+(W-1)\sum_{i,t}g_{i,t}\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}]\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}+(M-1)\sum_{i,t}g_{i,t}\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}]\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\right].

If the two activated proxy sets are respectively dominated by the corresponding entropy-increasing and entropy-decreasing quadrants, the expression reduces to

d​H¯d​η|V2,g=−1N​[Λ−(W−1)​Γg+−(1−M)​Γg−],\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{V2},g}=-\frac{1}{N}\bigl[\Lambda-(W-1)\Gamma_{g}^{+}-(1-M)\Gamma_{g}^{-}\bigr],

where

Γg−≜∑i,tgi,t𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq−]|A^iΦi,t|.\Gamma_{g}^{-}\triangleq\sum_{i,t}g_{i,t}\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}]|\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}|.
Proof.

The result follows by substituting the corresponding gated weights into the general weighted entropy identity derived in the proof of Proposition G.2. In the one-sided case,

ωi,t(V1,g)−1=gi,t(W−1)𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq+],\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{V1},g)}-1=g_{i,t}(W-1)\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}],

which gives

d​H¯d​η|V1,g=−1N[Λ+(W−1)∑i,tgi,t𝟏[(i,t)∈ℒq+]A^iΦi,t].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{V1},g}=-\frac{1}{N}\left[\Lambda+(W-1)\sum_{i,t}g_{i,t}\mathbf{1}[(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}]\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}\right].

The two-sided case follows by the same linearity argument. When the gated proxy sets preserve the dominant signs of their target quadrants, the corresponding signed sums can be rewritten as sums of absolute contributions. This proves the proposition. ∎

G.6 Unified Instantiations of Three Closed-Loop Granularities

The gate gi,tg_{i,t} in Proposition G.3 admits three closed-loop instantiations. For batch-level gating, define

gi,t(batch)=𝟏[H¯k<Htgt].g_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{batch})}=\mathbf{1}[\bar{H}_{k}<H_{\mathrm{tgt}}].

For sample-level gating, define

gi,t(sample)=𝟏[H¯i<Htgt],H¯i≜1Ti∑t=1TiHi,t.g_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{sample})}=\mathbf{1}[\bar{H}_{i}<H_{\mathrm{tgt}}],\qquad\bar{H}_{i}\triangleq\frac{1}{T_{i}}\sum_{t=1}^{T_{i}}H_{i,t}.

For token-level gating, define

gi,t(token)=𝟏[Hi,t<Htgt].g_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{token})}=\mathbf{1}[H_{i,t}<H_{\mathrm{tgt}}].

Because ωi,t>0\omega_{i,t}>0 holds in all three cases, every closed-loop variant preserves the direction of the original GRPO learning signal. The variants differ only in the granularity at which they modulate the local strength of the token-level update.

Appendix H Combined Reweighting Operations and Adaptive Weights

H.1 Exact Entropy Variation for Arbitrary Two-Subset Reweighting

Proposition H.1 (Exact entropy variation for arbitrary two-subset reweighting).

Let 𝒮1\mathcal{S}_{1} and 𝒮2\mathcal{S}_{2} be two disjoint token subsets. We assign multiplicative token weights r1>0r_{1}>0 and r2>0r_{2}>0 to them, respectively, while all remaining token positions receive unit weight:

ωi,t={r1,(i,t)∈𝒮1,r2,(i,t)∈𝒮2,1,otherwise.\omega_{i,t}=\begin{cases}r_{1},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{S}_{1},\\ r_{2},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{S}_{2},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}

Then, in the unclipped regime of the weighted GRPO surrogate,

d​H¯d​η|𝒮1,r1;𝒮2,r2=−1N​[Λ+(r1−1)​Ξ​(𝒮1)+(r2−1)​Ξ​(𝒮2)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathcal{S}_{1},r_{1};\mathcal{S}_{2},r_{2}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(r_{1}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{S}_{1})+(r_{2}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{S}_{2})\Big].
Proof.

The proof follows directly from the same argument as Proposition G.2. By the linearity of multiplicative token weighting,

∑i,tωi,t​A^i​Φi,t=∑i,tA^i​Φi,t+(r1−1)​∑(i,t)∈𝒮1A^i​Φi,t+(r2−1)​∑(i,t)∈𝒮2A^i​Φi,t.\sum_{i,t}\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}=\sum_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}+(r_{1}-1)\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{S}_{1}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}+(r_{2}-1)\sum_{(i,t)\in\mathcal{S}_{2}}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}.

Using the definitions of Λ\Lambda and Ξ⁡(⋅)\Xi(\cdot), this becomes

∑i,tωi,t​A^i​Φi,t=Λ+(r1−1)​Ξ​(𝒮1)+(r2−1)​Ξ​(𝒮2).\sum_{i,t}\omega_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i}\Phi_{i,t}=\Lambda+(r_{1}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{S}_{1})+(r_{2}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{S}_{2}).

Substituting this identity into the first-order batch-averaged entropy derivative yields the result. ∎

H.2 Four Representative Combined Reweighting Operations

We next instantiate Proposition H.1 for four representative two-subset reweighting schemes. Each scheme combines two single-polarity interventions from the four-quadrant entropy decomposition.

(1) Combination C1: amplifying ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} and amplifying 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-}.

C1 amplifies the two dominant entropy-increasing token categories on both advantage sides.

Define

ωi,t(C1)={W+,(i,t)∈ℒq+,W−,(i,t)∈𝒰q−,1,otherwise,W+>1,W−>1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{C1})}=\begin{cases}W_{+},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+},\\ W_{-},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad W_{+}>1,\quad W_{-}>1.

By Proposition H.1,

d​H¯d​η|C1=−1N​[Λ+(W+−1)​Ξ​(ℒq+)+(W−−1)​Ξ​(𝒰q−)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C1}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(W_{+}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+})+(W_{-}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-})\Big].

When the two proxy sets capture the dominant mass of their corresponding entropy-increasing quadrants, we have

d​H¯d​η|C1=−1N​[Λ−(W+−1)​ΓL+−(W−−1)​ΓU−].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C1}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(W_{+}-1)\Gamma_{L^{+}}-(W_{-}-1)\Gamma_{U^{-}}\Big].
(2) Combination C2: amplifying ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} and attenuating ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}.

C2 strengthens high-surprisal entropy-increasing tokens under positive advantages and weakens high-surprisal entropy-decreasing tokens under negative advantages. This is the combined operation used by Variant II in the main text.

Define

ωi,t(C2)={W,(i,t)∈ℒq+,M,(i,t)∈ℒq−,1,otherwise,W>1,0<M<1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{C2})}=\begin{cases}W,&(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+},\\ M,&(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad W>1,\quad 0<M<1.

By Proposition H.1,

d​H¯d​η|C2=−1N​[Λ+(W−1)​Ξ​(ℒq+)+(M−1)​Ξ​(ℒq−)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C2}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(W-1)\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+})+(M-1)\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-})\Big].

When the two proxy sets capture the dominant mass of the corresponding entropy-increasing and entropy-decreasing quadrants, respectively, we obtain

d​H¯d​η|C2=−1N​[Λ−(W−1)​ΓL+−(1−M)​ΓL−].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C2}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(W-1)\Gamma_{L^{+}}-(1-M)\Gamma_{L^{-}}\Big].

This expression matches the Variant II batch entropy shift in the main text:

ΛV2=Λ−(W−1)​Γ+−(1−M)​Γ−,\Lambda_{\mathrm{V2}}=\Lambda-(W-1)\Gamma^{+}-(1-M)\Gamma^{-},

where

Γ+=ΓL+,Γ−=ΓL−.\Gamma^{+}=\Gamma_{L^{+}},\qquad\Gamma^{-}=\Gamma_{L^{-}}.
(3) Combination C3: attenuating 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} and amplifying 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-}.

C3 regulates the low-surprisal region from both advantage sides. It weakens the entropy-decreasing signal from positive-advantage low-surprisal tokens and strengthens the entropy-increasing signal from negative-advantage low-surprisal tokens.

Define

ωi,t(C3)={M+,(i,t)∈𝒰q+,W−,(i,t)∈𝒰q−,1,otherwise,0<M+<1,W−>1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{C3})}=\begin{cases}M_{+},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+},\\ W_{-},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad 0<M_{+}<1,\quad W_{-}>1.

By Proposition H.1,

d​H¯d​η|C3=−1N​[Λ+(M+−1)​Ξ​(𝒰q+)+(W−−1)​Ξ​(𝒰q−)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C3}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(M_{+}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+})+(W_{-}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-})\Big].

When the proxy sets align with their target quadrants and capture the dominant contributions, we have

d​H¯d​η|C3=−1N​[Λ−(1−M+)​ΓU+−(W−−1)​ΓU−].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C3}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(1-M_{+})\Gamma_{U^{+}}-(W_{-}-1)\Gamma_{U^{-}}\Big].
(4) Combination C4: attenuating 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} and attenuating ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}.

C4 attenuates the two dominant entropy-decreasing token categories.

Define

ωi,t(C4)={M+,(i,t)∈𝒰q+,M−,(i,t)∈ℒq−,1,otherwise,0<M+<1,0<M−<1.\omega_{i,t}^{(\mathrm{C4})}=\begin{cases}M_{+},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+},\\ M_{-},&(i,t)\in\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-},\\ 1,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad 0<M_{+}<1,\quad 0<M_{-}<1.

By Proposition H.1,

d​H¯d​η|C4=−1N​[Λ+(M+−1)​Ξ​(𝒰q+)+(M−−1)​Ξ​(ℒq−)].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C4}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda+(M_{+}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+})+(M_{-}-1)\Xi(\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-})\Big].

When the two proxy sets capture the dominant mass of their corresponding entropy-decreasing quadrants, we obtain

d​H¯d​η|C4=−1N​[Λ−(1−M+)​ΓU+−(1−M−)​ΓL−].\left.\frac{d\bar{H}}{d\eta}\right|_{\mathrm{C4}}=-\frac{1}{N}\Big[\Lambda-(1-M_{+})\Gamma_{U^{+}}-(1-M_{-})\Gamma_{L^{-}}\Big].

H.3 Summary of Single-Polarity and Combined Operations

For clarity, we summarize the single-polarity operations O1 to O4 and the combined operations C1 to C4 below.

Single-polarity operations act on one entropy quadrant:

  • •

    O1 amplifies ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}, the positive-advantage high-surprisal set. It strengthens the entropy-increasing minority under positive advantages.

  • •

    O2 attenuates 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+}, the positive-advantage low-surprisal set. It weakens the dominant entropy-decreasing signal under positive advantages.

  • •

    O3 amplifies 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-}, the negative-advantage low-surprisal set. It strengthens the entropy-increasing effect induced by suppressing low-surprisal tokens.

  • •

    O4 attenuates ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}, the negative-advantage high-surprisal set. It weakens the entropy-decreasing effect induced by suppressing high-surprisal tokens.

Under the four-quadrant analysis in Section 3.2, O1 and O3 amplify entropy-increasing signals, whereas O2 and O4 attenuate entropy-decreasing signals. Variant I in the main text is a direct instance of O1, since it only amplifies token weights in ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+}.

Combined operations act on two entropy quadrants:

  • •

    C1 jointly amplifies ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} and 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-}. It strengthens entropy-increasing signals on both the positive- and negative-advantage sides.

  • •

    C2 amplifies ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} and attenuates ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}. It simultaneously strengthens positive-advantage high-surprisal entropy-increasing tokens and weakens negative-advantage high-surprisal entropy-decreasing tokens.

  • •

    C3 attenuates 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} and amplifies 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-}. It regulates the low-surprisal region by weakening positive-advantage entropy-decreasing tokens and strengthening negative-advantage entropy-increasing tokens.

  • •

    C4 jointly attenuates 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} and ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}. It suppresses the two dominant entropy-decreasing token categories.

Variant II in the main text is a representative instance of C2. It combines amplification of ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} with attenuation of ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-}. Since all weights remain positive, the sign of each original GRPO policy-gradient update is preserved. The method only rescales token-level contribution magnitudes, thereby regulating batch-level entropy dynamics through two complementary mechanisms: amplifying entropy-increasing contributions and attenuating entropy-decreasing contributions.

Single-polarity operations implement targeted interventions on individual entropy quadrants, while combined operations perform joint regulation across two quadrants.

Here, ℒq+\mathcal{L}_{q}^{+} and ℒq−\mathcal{L}_{q}^{-} denote high-surprisal proxy subsets within positive- and negative-advantage tokens, respectively, while 𝒰q+\mathcal{U}_{q}^{+} and 𝒰q−\mathcal{U}_{q}^{-} denote low-surprisal proxy subsets within positive- and negative-advantage tokens. Amplification refers to assigning weights larger than one, whereas attenuation refers to assigning weights in (0,1)(0,1).

Appendix I Limitations and Broader Impacts

Our empirical evaluation may not exhaustively cover all possible task distributions and optimization settings. Moreover, similar to other LLMs, our trained model could also generate potentially unethical or misleading information sometimes. We hope our work contributes positively to the development of more reliable post-training paradigms for large language models.
